rule.description: A member of a trait declared in this crate must not be handed to an implementor (or shipped as a provided body) as a do-nothing placeholder: a required member satisfied with a trivial body (returns self unchanged, a bare non-boolean literal, None, an empty container, or an empty block, including let-noise wrappers and zero-argument clones), or a provided member with a trivial body that an implementor inherits without overriding. Bodies that forward to another object or perform real per-device work do not violate the rule.

checks.description: Every function member of a locally declared trait is examined per implementor: a member that a device cannot meaningfully implement and that is satisfied by a do-nothing body (or by a do-nothing provided body the device inherits) is a placeholder that only exists to keep a fat interface uniform.
checks.detected_relation: implementor -> trait member provided as a do-nothing placeholder
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The fat interface is correctly split into focused, cohesive interfaces only when no implementor is required (or able) to satisfy members with placeholder bodies. The rule enumerates every (implementor, member) pair of each crate-local trait so the placeholder obligations are visible regardless of which class they sit in, and so moving a placeholder body into a trait default is still detected as an inherited placeholder rather than disappearing from view.
